Network distance downstream to the first river of each size, on each flow source

Source: R/link_walks.R
knw_link_walks.Rd

scripts/0296's walks. From a point on an FWA blue line, the path is walked downstream on route measures (inst/sql/ch_dist_profile.sql, the walk scripts/0294 fixed for one river size, for an array of sizes) to the first primary-flow segment whose annual flow on src is at least each q in q_grid. One row per start, source and size: status is found, none (the sea first), no_parent or too_many_hops. Side channels, connectors and other secondary-flow edges are passed over; a lake segment counts, as it would in a link rule.

Usage

knw_link_walks(
  connector,
  starts,
  q_grid = c(1, 3, 5, 10, 20, 30, 50),
  sources = c("pick", "pcic_routed", "wet_balance"),
  workers = 4L,
  batch = 500L,
  cache = FALSE
)

Arguments

connector

a function of no arguments returning a DBI connection to a database holding discharge and whse_basemapping.

starts

data.frame with blue_line_key and downstream_route_measure.

q_grid

numeric river sizes (m³/s), walked to in one pass.

sources

character flow sources: pick (wet's default per segment), pcic_routed, wet_balance.

workers

integer(1) socket workers.

batch

integer(1) starts per query. On the database's host a batch of 500 removes the round trip and R's per-row binding; over a remote link it removes almost all of a walk's time.

cache

FALSE (the default: walk everything), or a table name, schema.table, to read walks from and keep them in (see above).

Value

A tibble: blue_line_key, downstream_route_measure, src, qmin, status, dist_m, large_mad, large_lfid, large_edge, large_waterbody_key, n_hops, max_entry_gap_m, dist_centre_m, bank_m; exactly nrow(unique(starts)) * length(sources) * length(q_grid) rows. With a cache, attribute cache holds the start-and-source pairs read (hit) and walked (miss).

Details

The distance ends at the river's bank, by the rule fresh's frs_near_river() applies (#73): where the river found lies in a waterbody polygon, the connector segments (FWA edge types 1400 and 1450) the walk passed inside that polygon and the part of each hop's jump that crosses it are left out, and a connector inside a polygon the walk only passes through stays in. dist_centre_m is the distance to the centreline and bank_m what the rule took off it, so dist_m = pmax(dist_centre_m - bank_m, 0). What remains different from fresh's walk: this one starts where it is told (a visit's own point; the grade starts it at a segment's downstream end), crosses watershed-group outlets, and walks a line with no local code.

Each socket worker opens its own connection through connector and installs the walk as a session-temporary function, so a DBI connection cannot be passed: it does not serialise to a worker. A worker sends one query per batch starts and source (#87): the starts go to the server as two arrays, unnested with their position and walked laterally, and each row comes back tagged with its start's position, so the start's own values are attached in R and no key or measure is matched by its printed form. Every start must come back with one row per size. The result does not depend on batch: each start is walked alone, as before.

With cache a table name, every walk is kept (#87): a walk depends only on its start, the river size, the flow source, the flow load (knw_discharge_load(), by its md5) and the walk's code (knw_walk_md5()), so a row keyed on all six is the walk's own for as long as those hold. The starts go to a temporary table and the rows already kept are read with one join per 500,000 starts; a start missing any size on a source is walked for every size on that source (each size's result is independent of the others), and each batch's rows are inserted by the same query that walks them. The cache and its table of flow loads (<cache>_load) are created when absent. Rows under another load or walk are never read, and nothing prunes them. The FWA tables the walk reads carry no load record, so a reload of whse_basemapping.fwa_stream_networks_sp (fwapg#43 moves measures by millimetres) or of the river, lake, manmade waterbody and wetland polygons it measures the bank on needs the cache truncated by hand.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
pg <- function() DBI::dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres(), bigint = "numeric")
knw_link_walks(pg, data.frame(blue_line_key = 360886335, downstream_route_measure = 1520),
               q_grid = c(3, 10), sources = "pick", workers = 1)
} # }
